audience.text: C++ developers building desktop or server applications on Windows, Linux, or macOS who need to process Excel .xlsx files without external dependencies or licensing costs.

capabilities.text: The library supports creating blank workbooks and saving them to .xlsx format using Workbook constructors and Save methods.
capabilities.title: Create and save .xlsx workbooks

capabilities.text: Cell.PutValue() accepts strings, integers, doubles, booleans, and DateTime; Cell.SetFormula() and Cell.GetFormula() handle Excel formula text.
capabilities.title: Read and write cell values and formulas

capabilities.text: Style objects bundle font, fill, borders, alignment, and number format settings applied via Cell.GetStyle() and Cell.SetStyle().
capabilities.title: Apply cell and range styling

capabilities.text: The library supports worksheet protection, visibility control, page setup, hyperlinks, defined names, conditional formatting, and data validation.
capabilities.title: Manage worksheet features

capabilities.text: Core and extended document properties are accessible through WorkbookProperties and DocumentProperties objects.
capabilities.title: Configure document properties

capabilities.text: Conditional formatting rules and data validation constraints are managed via FormatCondition and Validation objects applied to cell ranges.
capabilities.title: Support conditional formatting and validation

capabilities.text: AutoFilter functionality including custom filters, dynamic filters, top 10 rules, and sort conditions is exposed through AutoFilter objects.
capabilities.title: Handle AutoFilter and sorting

capabilities.text: The library is built using CMake with a minimum version of 3.16 and targets C++17 without external dependencies.
capabilities.title: Build with CMake

limitations.text: Only .xlsx (OOXML) format is supported for loading and saving; saving to other formats throws UnsupportedFeatureException.
Legacy SpreadsheetML (Excel 2003 XML) is not implemented; mapper classes for it unconditionally throw UnsupportedFeatureException.
Cell-level comments/notes are not modeled as a distinct object; only DefinedName has a Comment field.
Some advanced conditional-formatting rule types are dropped with a WarningInfo during load rather than preserved.
AutoFilter date-group filters using certain patterns are rejected as unsupported during load.
Prebuilt NuGet packages are available only for Windows with MSVC toolset; Linux and macOS require building from source.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic Excel workbook creation and manipulation in C++ without requiring Microsoft Excel or commercial licensing.
Provides a consistent API surface compatible with Aspose.Cells commercial products for common spreadsheet operations.
Supports cross-platform development with a header-and-source C++17 library that compiles on MSVC, GCC, and Clang.

product_summary.text: Aspose.Cells FOSS for C++ is a dependency-free, open-source C++17 library for creating, loading, editing, and saving Excel .xlsx workbooks without requiring Microsoft Excel.

uncertainties: The exact set of supported conditional formatting rule types that are preserved versus dropped is not fully specified beyond 'some advanced' types.
The behavior of Workbook constructors when loading corrupted or partially valid .xlsx files is not detailed beyond InvalidFileFormatException.
Whether the library supports reading or writing .xlsb or .ods formats is not explicitly confirmed beyond stating only .xlsx is supported.

workflows.name: Create and save workbooks
workflows.text: Developers instantiate a Workbook, add worksheets, populate cells with values and formulas, apply styles, and save to .xlsx using Workbook.Save().

workflows.name: Load and read existing workbooks
workflows.text: Developers load existing .xlsx files from disk or memory streams and read cell values, formulas, and metadata.

workflows.name: Apply formatting and styling
workflows.text: Developers apply cell styles including font properties, fill patterns, borders, alignment, and number formats to cells and ranges.

workflows.name: Configure worksheet features
workflows.text: Developers manage visibility, protection, page setup, hyperlinks, defined names, conditional formatting, and data validation on worksheets.
